title: Retry safety follows operation semantics, not HTTP method alone
summary: Non-idempotent submissions must not be replayed after ambiguous acceptance. Generic Fabric JSON mutations now skip gateway retries; selected Fabric/Power BI JSON and job paths retain bounded error.submission evidence with retriable:false. Safe reads keep their intended retry policy.
policy: Generic Fabric post/post_empty distinguish Mutation from explicit ReadOnly semantics. Mutations never automatically retry 502/503/504 or network failures. Explicit read-only POSTs (such as catalog search, the shared get-definition helper and Activator query) retain the existing bounded gateway retries, as do safe GETs. No action-name substring chooses retry safety at runtime.

Existing auth refresh after 401 and bounded Fabric 429/430 rejection retries remain only without contradictory Location/operation markers. Fabric generic throttling retries honor Retry-After up to 300 seconds with at most three retries. Some senders have stricter policies: Gen1 submits exactly once even on 401/429/5xx, and notebook's one-attempt sender remains one attempt. Do not infer idempotence from the HTTP status, operation name or a server isRetriable flag.

Generic Fabric JSON, configurable-LRO JSON, job triggers and Power BI JSON mutation failures carry optional error.submission when acceptance is unknown or a successful acknowledgement cannot be decoded/observed. retriable:false and semantic_correction prevent replay even when the API said isRetriable:true. Existing API code/parameters/details/trace remain intact; submission.serverRetriable retains the server hint separately.

Command-level retry loops for named rejection conditions (deployment name reservation, mirrored-database readiness and Git initialization) also reject errors carrying submission evidence or retriable:false. A matching message alone must not trigger another POST after ambiguous acceptance. Git checkout likewise does not reconnect the previous branch after an uncertain reconnect response; that could undo a switch already accepted.
evidence: submission.state is accepted for HTTP 202, acknowledged for other successful responses whose later handling failed, and unknown for transport failure/408/5xx, unexpected redirect/nonstandard statuses or contradictory markers. This is diagnostic evidence, not a local ledger receipt, proof of remote completion or verified batch scope.

Only a unique, well-formed nonzero x-ms-operation-id header can populate submission.operationId; traces and Location strings never become operation IDs here. locationPresent is only a boolean. Requested workspace/target UUIDs are retained when the route supplies them; bodies, arbitrary names, query strings and returned URLs are not copied into this object. Multi-item body scope is not reconstructed.

Preserve the original exact request and evidence privately. Inspect the same operation/resource with the correct configured service and GET-only tooling. Never guess an ID, pass a transport operation ID as a local receipt ID, use latest-history matching, automatically resubmit or turn observation failure into cancellation.

deploy apply retains legacy failures[].change/error/code and adds canonical errorDetails for typed failures plus retryAllowed:false for every failed action and recorded hook error. The batch's retryAllowed:false/no-replay hint dominates nested retriable:true and diagnosticHint: an action may have successful substeps. Preserve the result, reconcile read-only and review a new scoped plan before further mutation; never replay the entire batch automatically.

Bulk request errors shared across action records describe one request, not proof each item failed remotely. Only unique complete Succeeded results with nonzero item IDs count as success; Failed/SucceededDespiteFailures remain failures and missing/duplicate/contradictory/unknown rows become BULK_RESULT_UNVERIFIED without invented transport evidence. Do not switch strategy or disconnect Git after uncertain submission. Nonfatal recorded hook failures keep existing status/exit behavior, so status:succeeded is not proof every hook succeeded.
limits: This is a bounded transport audit, not a universal exactly-once or end-to-end idempotence guarantee. Raw text/binary/multipart/ARM/OneLake/custom HTTP/SDK paths and bespoke definition-retrieval callers are not all migrated to the new contextual error contract. No newly verified idempotent mutation exception or idempotency key is invented.

Deployment prerequisite failures halt remaining actions/deletes with halted:true/notExecuted; recorded hook failures stop later hook mutations. Successful inter-tier refreshes are not repeated. Shortcut reconciliation refuses malformed/partial inventories and stops on failed mutations. Other batch summaries and specialized transports remain separately scoped. Absence of evidence is not proof of rejection; no remote recovery heuristic is implied.
